steps: Split a composite request into independently verifiable work items.
Apply human-policy-authority and other hard-stop routes before specialist matching.
Match the most specific route whose when conditions fit and whose exclusions do not fit.
Use priority only after specificity; do not route a specialist task back to the owner Skill merely because it can discuss the topic.
Verify candidate availability in the active Skill catalog before invocation and read the selected Skill instructions.
If no named candidate is available, discover by capability tags or return a visible missing-capability handoff; never silently absorb the work.
Return every specialist result to the owner Skill for workflow-semantic reconciliation and acceptance.
candidate_availability: Prefer an exact candidate Skill ID that is present in the active session.
Otherwise select an available Skill whose description matches the route discovery tags and required output.
Do not install a missing Skill unless the user explicitly requests installation.
Do not treat a candidate name in this registry as proof that the capability is installed or suitable.

when: A business rule, policy, approval owner, decision right, acceptance standard, release, deletion, publication, or external commitment is unresolved.
The requested automation would cause AI to make a decision reserved for an accountable human.
exclusions: The authority rule is already accepted and the task only represents it online without changing its meaning.
required_inputs: The exact unresolved decision.
The affected workflow objects, states, people, and consequences.
Reversible work that can proceed without the decision.
expected_outputs: An explicit human decision or a recorded pending decision with owner and deadline.
A statement of which implementation work remains blocked.
routes.human_boundary: Only the named accountable human may decide, approve, release, delete, publish, or commit externally.
validation: No default policy or approval has been invented.
Dependent automation remains blocked or explicitly non-canon until the decision exists.
routes.integration_destination: Transformation contract, authority map, decision register, and affected Gate or migration plan.
routes.fallback: Stop the dependent work, surface the decision request, and continue only reversible independent work.

when: The correctness, safety, legality, or professional validity of an industry/domain method must be judged before digitization.
Conflicting domain practices cannot be resolved from accepted project evidence.
exclusions: The domain method is already accepted and the task only structures or governs its execution.
required_inputs: The disputed method or claim.
Applicable jurisdiction, industry, evidence, and project boundary.
The workflow decision that depends on the answer.
expected_outputs: A bounded professional judgment with sources, assumptions, and uncertainty.
An accepted rule or a clearly unresolved domain decision.
routes.human_boundary: A domain specialist or accountable human approves the method; the workflow Skill does not certify professional correctness.
validation: The judgment is evidence-backed and scoped to the applicable context.
Uncertainty and prohibited automation are explicit.
routes.integration_destination: Accepted-rule register, evidence ledger, workflow model, and AI eligibility decision.
routes.fallback: Record the method as unresolved and keep dependent online or AI behavior disabled.

when: The selected online model requires custom application, product experience, API, database, identity, permissions, security, queue, deployment, or infrastructure design.
A codebase or AI product architecture must be created or materially refactored.
exclusions: The task is limited to file-based workflow governance covered by the bundled contract and scripts.

candidate_skills.use_when: User journeys, product scope, requirements, and implementation-ready product decisions are needed.
An AI-native product, Agent platform, Copilot, or model/tool boundary needs architecture review.
A major code/system architecture audit or refactor is required.
A software repository needs a governed AI coding environment before implementation.

required_inputs: Accepted AS-IS and TO-BE workflow semantics.
Work objects, states, actions, authority, exceptions, and non-functional constraints.
Scope exclusions and required integration points.
expected_outputs: A product or technical architecture within the accepted workflow boundary.
Implementation plan, risks, interfaces, and verification evidence.
routes.human_boundary: Product scope, security posture, budget, and irreversible architecture choices require accountable human approval.
validation: The architecture implements rather than silently changes accepted workflow semantics.
Interfaces, failure behavior, permissions, migration, and rollback are testable.
routes.integration_destination: TO-BE operating model, implementation plan, runtime chain, migration record, and acceptance test.
routes.fallback: Deliver the workflow and integration contract only; mark custom implementation as a missing specialist capability.

when: A stable online-tested workflow must become a reusable installable Skill.
Skill metadata, resources, scripts, evals, installation, discovery, or forward testing must be implemented.
exclusions: The workflow has not been online-tested or its capability and human boundaries remain unresolved.

candidate_skills.use_when: Create or update the Skill package, metadata, resources, validation, and evals.

required_inputs: Proven workflow capability boundary.
Accepted inputs, outputs, allowed actions, human decisions, runtime assumptions, and failure modes.
Representative positive, negative, and handoff scenarios.
expected_outputs: A lean Skill package with only required instructions and resources.
Validation, realistic evals, installation or discovery evidence, and forward-test results where appropriate.
routes.human_boundary: The human retains approval over package scope, installation, publication, and any widened authority.
validation: The package passes its format and resource checks.
Evals test observed failure modes and do not assume unproven workflow adoption.
routes.integration_destination: Capability registry, runtime entrypoint, transformation acceptance record, and knowledge backflow.
routes.fallback: Keep the workflow specification and packaging handoff; do not fabricate an installed or tested Skill.

when: The accepted workflow must be implemented through a named enterprise collaboration platform such as Feishu/Lark or DingTalk.
Platform-specific records, approvals, tasks, documents, tables, messages, or calendars must be created or changed.
exclusions: The user only needs a platform-neutral workflow model or template pack.

candidate_skills.use_when: A Feishu/Lark custom app or hosted application is required.
The online work object should be represented in Feishu/Lark Base.
An already-approved approval policy must be represented or operated in Feishu/Lark.
Accepted work items should be created or managed as Feishu/Lark tasks.
The target platform is DingTalk and its supported workflow capabilities fit the task.

required_inputs: Named target platform and authorized tenant or workspace boundary.
Accepted work objects, states, fields, permissions, and human approval rules.
Allowed external mutations and rollback plan.
expected_outputs: Platform-specific implementation mapped to the accepted online model.
Created or changed object IDs, validation evidence, and remaining platform gaps.
routes.human_boundary: Tenant access, messages, approvals, external writes, and production changes follow explicit user authority and platform permissions.
validation: Platform objects and fields preserve the accepted workflow meaning.
External writes, IDs, permissions, and rollback evidence are recorded.
routes.integration_destination: Online object registry, runtime entrypoint, migration record, and operational acceptance evidence.
routes.fallback: Produce a platform-neutral mapping and identify the unavailable platform capability without claiming deployment.

when: The workflow requires a structured knowledge base, knowledge architecture, content migration, or knowledge-quality release beyond simple backflow records.
exclusions: The task only registers a small evidence-backed reusable lesson in the existing knowledge destination.

candidate_skills.use_when: Audit, design, restructure, or build a governed knowledge base.

required_inputs: Knowledge users, questions, sources, permissions, lifecycle, and destination.
Project evidence and confidentiality or reuse boundaries.
expected_outputs: A governed knowledge structure or migration within the accepted scope.
Source traceability, lifecycle states, quality checks, and release evidence.
routes.human_boundary: Humans approve confidentiality, copyright, publication, de-identification, and knowledge validity claims.
validation: Knowledge claims retain source and applicability boundaries.
Project facts are not silently promoted to universal guidance.
routes.integration_destination: Knowledge-backflow register, source registry, navigation, and closure evidence.
routes.fallback: Keep evidence-backed backflow candidates inside the project and mark knowledge-system work pending.

when: The selected workflow output must be produced in a specialized file format or edited in a live productivity application.
Document, spreadsheet, presentation, PDF, or visual fidelity is itself part of acceptance.
exclusions: A plain Markdown workflow contract or simple copy-ready template is sufficient.

candidate_skills.use_when: Create or edit professional Word-compatible documents.
Create, edit, analyze, or validate spreadsheets.
Read, create, inspect, or render governed PDF outputs.

required_inputs: Approved content, format, template, destination, and fidelity criteria.
No-edit regions, source versions, and output authority.
expected_outputs: The requested artifact in the required format.
Visual or structural validation evidence and source-version traceability.
routes.human_boundary: Humans approve externally distributed content and any substantive business claims; the format specialist does not invent them.
validation: The artifact matches the approved source and format requirements.
No-edit content and version lineage remain intact.
routes.integration_destination: Artifact registry, active-version record, Gate evidence, and delivery or release package.
routes.fallback: Return the approved content and format handoff without pretending the specialized artifact was produced.

when: The task is AS-IS recovery, digitization-profile assessment, shared workflow modeling, file-based governance, state/version/Gate design, migration, repair, AI-node boundary, pilot, acceptance, or backflow integration within accepted semantics.
exclusions: A higher-priority human or specialist route applies to the same work item.

candidate_skills.use_when: Own the transformation contract, workflow model, routing, integration, migration, and acceptance.

required_inputs: Accepted workflow evidence or a bounded guided-start target.
Current and target digitization profile, authority effects, scope, exclusions, and adoption/acceptance evidence.
expected_outputs: The smallest transformation artifact needed by the selected action.
Visible unresolved decisions, specialist handoffs, validation, and rollback when applicable.
routes.human_boundary: The Skill may structure accepted work but may not invent policy, approve release, or widen authority.
validation: Preserved and changed workflow semantics are explicit.
No higher-priority specialist work was silently absorbed.
routes.integration_destination: Canonical online operating model and transformation acceptance record.
routes.fallback: Return to guided-start or a read-only audit; do not fabricate missing workflow facts.
